Subject: Request for additional eval credits and consolidation of pilot accounts

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at KyberWorks is excited to push a larger eval across our clinical NLP and search squads. We’re about to spin up three additional sandbox projects and will likely blow through the credits you provisioned.

Could we get an additional 200k tokens for the next 14 days? I’ve attached the current usage CSV and a short note from our engineering lead that shows planned parallel runs. We’re a small mid-market shop but with four separate teams running short pilots it’s a legit burst.

I should also flag that Legal has asked about a short MPA addendum — they’ll attach if needed. We’re happy to sign if there are guardrails (rate limits, data retention).

Thanks,
Amit

Amit — appreciate the context and the usage file. Quick follow-up before I approve anything:

- Can you confirm whether the four sandboxes are under the same company/org in your signups or if they’re separate accounts?
- We’ve seen cases where teams create multiple trials to extend credits; to avoid that we review sequences of top-ups across accounts.

Looping in Marissa (ops) and Neha (fraud/compliance) to triage. If everything looks legitimate we can do a one-time augmentation or a short extension. If there are multiple account topups we’ll need to document and escalate to our policy team.

Proposed next step: I’ll ask Ops to pull the server-side topup history and Neha to surface any patterns. Can you also share the engineering lead’s note (if different from the MPA request)?

—Sean

Forwarding Amit’s request and the usage dump. I ran a quick ops pull and attached a CSV of account topup events across the last 90 days. Highlights:

- Four distinct account IDs tied to the kyberworks.ai org (two share an email domain pattern, two are on generic gmail addresses).
- Topups occurred on 2026-05-12, 2026-06-09, 2026-07-01 and 2026-07-20; amounts are small but frequent (multiple 25k token grants).
- IPs for two accounts are overlapping and the user agent strings are identical across sessions.

This looks like a parallel pilot approach but it also matches patterns we logged in previous promo-loop incidents (multiple small grants to extend evaluation window). Attaching evidence_topup_log.csv. Recommend fraud review before approving blanket credits.

-Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KyberWorks usage — fraud signal and recommendation

Thanks for the data — ran a quick cross-account correlation. Short summary:

- Two accounts appear to be legitimate (company email domains, matching org metadata).
- Two accounts are suspicious: generic addresses, repeated small topups within 48–72 hour windows, overlapping IPs, identical UA strings.
- No evidence of stolen payment methods; token grants appear to be promo/comp credits requested via support flows rather than chargebacks.

Recommendation: Put a temporary hold on auto-provisioning more eval promo credits to any accounts under the cluster while we request verification. Offer KyberWorks a monitored 3-day extension on their primary account (that we can revert) and ask for a short attestation: list of team members, intended workload, and confirmation that these aren’t parallel accounts set up to extend trials. If they provide an MPA addendum and an SOC2 timeline we can consider a one-time consolidated credit after legal review.

I’m marking this as "suspicious-pattern" internally and will prepare evidence for the policy queue if they attempt to claim multiple promo grants in quick succession.

-Ben

[Attachment: fraud_flags_summary.txt (text/plain)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: KyberWorks — request for additional evaluation credits / usage pattern review

Amit — thanks for your patience. Quick update after our internal review:

We can’t automatically grant the 200k token augmentation requested across the four accounts. Our fraud ops team observed a cluster of small top-ups and overlapping signals between two of the accounts that match known promo-extension patterns. To protect the program we need a short verification step.

What we can offer immediately:
- A monitored 72-hour extension on your primary company account (no new promo credits to the other accounts during this window).
- If you complete and return a short attestation (list of pilot team members and intended workloads) and provide confirmation that the other accounts belong to the same organizational entity, we’ll fast-track a one-time consolidated credit. We’ll also accept a signed MPA addendum (Legal).

Please attach the attestation and MPA to this thread. For convenience I’ve included a DocuSign link for a simple addendum. Once legal and fraud sign off we’ll post the consolidated credit and open the Dedicated capacity discussion you mentioned.

If you prefer, we can also set up a 15-minute call with Neha and Marissa to walk through the evidence and next steps.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you unblocked.

—Sean
